mission_06: While MAML was originally demonstrated on sinusoidal regression, its most impactful application is few-shot classification. Adapting MAML for classification requires replacing the MSE loss with cross-entropy loss and using softmax outputs. The inner loop adapts parameters on the support set using cross-entropy: L = -sum(y_onehot * log(softmax(logits))). The gradient of cross-entropy with respect to logits is elegantly simple: dL/dz = softmax(z) - y_onehot. For few-shot classification, MAML is typically evaluated on benchmarks like Omniglot (handwritten characters from 50 alphabets) and miniImageNet (100 image classes). The N-way K-shot setting means each episode has N classes with K support examples per class. MAML learns an initialization that can be quickly adapted to recognize new classes with very few examples, making it powerful for scenarios where labeled data is scarce.
